investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-19T03:26–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before a VM can be allocated, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain missing. This is a cluster-capacity or peer-pod resource exhaustion condition, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 147s.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149809, confirming the check timed out waiting for scheduling, not a transient API error.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the runner never reaching the VM-allocation step.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming no agent was created.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=154899, evidenceKeys=[] — same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=149760, evidenceKeys=[] — same root cause.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returns successfully because the pod cannot be scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because no VM was allocated.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: both peer-pod-capable nodes are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node selector or affinity rules, permanently reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes regardless of capacity.

Tertiary — no preemption path available: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning lower-priority pods on the 2 eligible nodes cannot be evicted to free capacity.

Lower probability — a previous eval run or other workload left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (e.g., a cleanup failure in withCleanup at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster immediately to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation across all nodes; if exhausted, identify and terminate any orphaned or long-running remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up by the eval runner's withCleanup handler.

Review the node affinity and selector configuration on the remote-agent pod template to determine whether the restriction to 2 nodes is intentional or whether additional nodes could be labeled to expand the schedulable pool.

Investigate whether the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is reliably releasing kata.peerpods.io/vm resources after each probe run, particularly in failure and timeout scenarios.
If capacity exhaustion is confirmed as sustained, escalate to the infrastructure team to either add kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on additional nodes or increase the per-node VM slot limit.
This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity condition; do not treat it as a user-facing outage unless independent traffic or incident signals confirm end-user impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available (i.e., allocatable > used) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would be misleading and the true cause lies elsewhere in the pod spec or admission configuration.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have the correct node labels and the affinity rules are misconfigured in the pod template, the primary cause would be a node-selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no orphaned remote-agent VMs are found on the cluster and capacity is confirmed free, the root cause may be a peer-pod provider quota or external VM pool limit rather than a Kubernetes-level resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes and alerts before full exhaustion (e.g., warn when utilization exceeds 80%).
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent VMs remain allocated after each remote-agent probe cycle.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), catching pool-shrinkage regressions before they cause full scheduling failures.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check inside the remote-agent-create runner branch that fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhausted message rather than waiting for the full pod-stuck timeout (currently ~147–154s).

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T03:28–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable with the message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a pod reaching a running state before it can collect any evidence; the scheduling failure prevents that entirely, causing all four required evidence fields to be absent and the check to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires exactly [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none were present.
possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

Secondary (medium confidence): The node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a hard ceiling on concurrent VM capacity. If those 2 nodes are sized for a fixed number of peer-pod VMs, a burst of concurrent agent creation (e.g., from multiple eval runs or real workloads) could exhaust the resource.

Tertiary (low confidence): A previous eval run or a real user workload may have left orphaned agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released before this eval run started. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-19T03:26–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before a VM can be allocated, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, no evidence is written, and all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain missing. This is a cluster-capacity or peer-pod resource exhaustion condition, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149809, confirming the check timed out waiting for scheduling, not a transient API error.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the runner never reaching the VM-allocation step.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming no agent was created.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because no VM was allocated.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: both peer-pod-capable nodes are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node selector or affinity rules, permanently reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes regardless of capacity.

Tertiary — no preemption path available: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning lower-priority pods on the 2 eligible nodes cannot be evicted to free capacity.

Lower probability — a previous eval run or other workload left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (e.g., a cleanup failure in withCleanup at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster immediately to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation across all nodes; if exhausted, identify and terminate any orphaned or long-running remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up by the eval runner's withCleanup handler.

Review the node affinity and selector configuration on the remote-agent pod template to determine whether the restriction to 2 nodes is intentional or whether additional nodes could be labeled to expand the schedulable pool.

If capacity exhaustion is confirmed as sustained, escalate to the infrastructure team to either add kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on additional nodes or increase the per-node VM slot limit.
This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity condition; do not treat it as a user-facing outage unless independent traffic or incident signals confirm end-user impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available (i.e., allocatable > used) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would be misleading and the true cause lies elsewhere in the pod spec or admission configuration.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have the correct node labels and the affinity rules are misconfigured in the pod template, the primary cause would be a node-selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no orphaned remote-agent VMs are found on the cluster and capacity is confirmed free, the root cause may be a peer-pod provider quota or external VM pool limit rather than a Kubernetes-level resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes and alerts before full exhaustion (e.g., warn when utilization exceeds 80%).
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent VMs remain allocated after each remote-agent probe cycle.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), catching pool-shrinkage regressions before they cause full scheduling failures.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check inside the remote-agent-create runner branch that fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhausted message rather than waiting for the full pod-stuck timeout (currently ~147–154s).

Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable with the message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

Secondary (medium confidence): The node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a hard ceiling on concurrent VM capacity. If those 2 nodes are sized for a fixed number of peer-pod VMs, a burst of concurrent agent creation (e.g., from multiple eval runs or real workloads) could exhaust the resource.

Tertiary (low confidence): A previous eval run or a real user workload may have left orphaned agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released before this eval run started. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is NOT exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling error message would need a different explanation.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passed (or if its pod was successfully scheduled) while remote-agent-state failed, the cause would be isolated to the state-polling logic rather than shared VM capacity.

If re-running the eval immediately after the failure window produces a passing result with no infrastructure changes, the failure may have been transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent usage) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 2 affinity-eligible nodes show zero kata.peerpods.io/vm consumption by existing pods, the root cause would shift to a node-level configuration error (e.g., the resource not being advertised correctly by the node plugin) rather than capacity exhaustion.
If no node in the cluster carries the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at all, the cause would be a missing or misconfigured peer-pod device plugin rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on affinity-eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before agent creation is attempted.

Add a stale-pod detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any have been running beyond the expected agent lifecycle duration, indicating a cleanup failure.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold, catching configuration drift that reduces the schedulable node pool.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between a scheduling failure (Unschedulable) and an API-level creation failure, so the failure message and evidence can be localized to the correct layer without waiting for the full timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-19T03:28–03:33Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled within the eval timeout window (~147–149 s), the remote agent VM was never provisioned, and the runtime check produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod is placed in the Unschedulable state immediately because 0/6 nodes can satisfy the request: 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod remains unscheduled for ~143–148 s until the eval timeout fires, leaving the evidence object empty and violating the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918 line 1918: createAgent is called with type 'remote', which triggers the kata/peerpods VM pod creation path that the scheduler cannot satisfy
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required affinity, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes are undersized or their VM quota is too low for concurrent eval runs, exhaustion is structurally inevitable.

TERTIARY — eval cleanup not releasing VM slots promptly: if prior remote-agent eval runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) did not fully clean up their kata/peerpods VMs before remote-agent-runtime ran, the 2 eligible nodes may have been saturated by the earlier sibling checks. The sequential timing (create ended 03:28, state ended 03:31, runtime started 03:31) is consistent with this.
LOWER CONFIDENCE — node pool scaling not triggered or too slow: the cluster may lack autoscaling for kata/peerpods-capable nodes, or the scale-up latency exceeds the eval timeout window.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message directly names kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes as the blocking condition for all three remote-agent eval pods.

affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire remote-agent provisioning path is blocked, not just the runtime check.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to confirm exhaustion and determine whether manual VM slot reclamation or node restart is needed.

Verify that the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is successfully releasing kata/peerpods VM resources after each sibling check (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) before the next check runs, to prevent cumulative slot starvation.

Assess whether the 2-node kata/peerpods pool is sized appropriately for concurrent or sequential eval runs; if not, coordinate with the infrastructure team to expand the pool or increase per-node VM quota.
Confirm whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are intentionally excluded (e.g., wrong machine type) or whether a configuration drift has incorrectly narrowed the eligible node set.

Add a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval probe that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting agent creation, and skips with a descriptive message if capacity is zero, to distinguish infrastructure unavailability from product regressions.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves VM slot exhaustion by showing current allocatable vs. used counts on each node, and identifies which 4 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether prior eval runs left orphaned pods consuming VM slots, supporting or refuting the cleanup-gap hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether only 2 nodes are structurally eligible for remote-agent pods and whether that pool size is intentional or a misconfiguration.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the pending pod showed a different failure reason (e.g., image pull error, OOMKilled, API auth failure) rather than Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, the VM exhaustion diagnosis would be wrong.

If the 2 kata/peerpods-capable nodes showed available VM slots at the time of the eval run, exhaustion would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration preventing the pod from landing on those nodes.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state sibling checks had passed (or if their pods were confirmed cleaned up before remote-agent-runtime ran), the cumulative slot consumption hypothesis would be weakened.

If no-history data (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) is explained by a newly registered check rather than a genuine regression, the failure may be a first-run infrastructure gap rather than a regression.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes and fails with a clear capacity signal before any remote-agent creation is attempted.
Add a post-cleanup verification step to each remote-agent eval check confirming that VM slots are released within a bounded time window after withCleanup completes.

Add a node-affinity/selector conformance eval that asserts the expected number of nodes (e.g., at least N) match the remote-agent pod's scheduling requirements, catching pool shrinkage before it causes eval failures.

Consider a serialization or rate-limiting guard in the eval runner so that remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime do not compete for the same limited VM slots within a single run.
